findings: Guesses drift to the slider's middle. On slider A the answer sat 70–84% along on four questions, and each time the median guess fell back towards the middle (only slightly on the World Cup, which people know). On B the answer sat near the middle and the median stayed with it.
The VW Beetles show it most. The median on slider A was exactly the slider's starting point, 3.16 million, 6.8 times too small. On B it was about 10% short of the answer.
caveats: B mostly tested "answer near the middle". So this says more about where the answer sits than about wider or narrower ends.
Knowledge still wins. The Return of the King scored about the same on both sliders (people know a film's length), and Athens to Istanbul came out too far on both.
B made the game easier. Higher scores are what you'd expect when the slider's starting point sits near the answer. Whether that's the game you want is a separate question from whether B works.
